caption.en: Raqqa, Syria, twelfth–thirteenth century, Ayyubid period. The museum catalogues this stone-paste pitcher as a waster: a rejected product.

interpretation.en: The collapsed shape records the risk behind finished ceramics. Black painting beneath blue glaze combined forming, decoration and firing, and some vessels failed in production. Raqqa is the catalogue attribution; its excavation context is unrecorded.
interpretation.zh: 塌陷形态记录了成品陶器背后的风险。蓝釉下的黑彩结合成形、装饰与烧制工序，有些器物在生产中失败。拉卡为目录所记产地，考古出土背景未载。

ledger.visualReview: Full source image inspected: seated central Buddha, eight attendants, patterned red-gold robe, darkened worn silk. No modern imagined likeness. Original temple/patron unidentified.

relationship.en: Gold patterns, translucent garments and a carefully ordered assembly make Buddhist devotion visible as skilled artistic work. The museum identifies Amita at the center and Kshitigarbha in the simpler hooded garment. This surviving Goryeo painting directly illustrates the religious arts described in the entry; its original patron and temple are not identified.
relationship.zh: 金色纹样、轻透衣饰与精心安排的群像，将佛教信仰化为精细的绘画劳动。馆方将中央尊像认定为阿弥陀佛，穿简朴兜帽衣袍者为地藏菩萨。这幅高丽遗存直接呈现条目所述宗教艺术；原始委托者与所属寺院尚未确定。

summary.en: Goryeo courts and aristocrats supported Buddhist institutions, whose temples sustained painting, sculpture and ritual crafts. Celadon pottery became a distinctive achievement, and cast-metal movable type appeared before its later European development. The kingdom also faced repeated pressure from neighboring powers, including Khitan and Mongol invasions. Cultural creativity therefore coexisted with military danger and difficult diplomacy. The capital at Songdo linked court life with wider religious and commercial networks. A change of ruling house in 1392 brought Joseon policies and a different ideological emphasis, rather than an end to Korean cultural traditions.
summary.zh: 高丽王室与贵族支持佛教寺院，促进绘画、雕塑和礼仪工艺发展。青瓷形成鲜明特色，金属活字的使用也早于后来欧洲的发展。与此同时，高丽面对契丹与蒙古等势力的侵袭，文化创造与军事压力、外交周旋并存。松都连接宫廷、宗教和商业网络；1392年的王朝更替带来朝鲜的新政策与思想重点，并非文化传统终止。

dateNote.en: 918–1392 follows the Met’s Goryeo chronology. The pin marks Songdo, now Gaeseong; influence and control varied through the period.
dateNote.zh: 918—1392年采用大都会博物馆年表；标记为松都，即今开城，实际控制随时期变化。

title.en: Ayyubids: a family of courts from Egypt to Syria
title.zh: 阿尤布王朝：从埃及到叙利亚的家族宫廷

summary.en:
Salah al-Din ended the Fatimid caliphate in Egypt in 1171 and established Ayyubid rule. His dynasty extended power into Yemen and Syria. Its territories were administered through related rulers and courts rather than one uniformly centralized state.

Religious education, fortifications and skilled metalwork formed part of this political world. Objects and craftsmen moved between cities, crossing the boundaries of rival rulers. The rise of the Mamluks ended independent Ayyubid rule in Egypt in 1250, while Syrian strongholds survived longer. This overlapping succession explains why a single “dynasty ended” date needs a location qualification.
summary.zh:
萨拉丁于1171年结束埃及法蒂玛哈里发统治，建立阿尤布政权。其王朝把权力伸向也门与叙利亚。领地通过有亲缘关系的统治者和多个宫廷治理，并非处处具有同样中央集权。

宗教教育、城防和精细金属工艺属于这一政治世界。物品与工匠在城市之间流动，跨越竞争统治者的边界。1250年马穆鲁克兴起，终结阿尤布在埃及的独立统治，但叙利亚据点继续存在一段时间。因此单一“王朝结束”日期需要地点限定。

dateNote.en: 1171–1260 follows the Met’s broad dynastic period. Egypt’s independent Ayyubid line ended in 1250; Syrian strongholds had another trajectory. Cairo is a representative early center, not the court of every ruler.
dateNote.zh: 1171—1260年采用大都会博物馆的宽泛王朝时期。埃及独立支系于1250年终结，叙利亚据点另有进程。开罗是代表性早期中心，不表示每位统治者的宫廷。

notes.label: Description
notes.content: Buddha and eight disciples. The Buddha is seated on a lotus throne aloft, in the attitude of teaching. His throne rests upon an alter decorated in lotus motive, and before this and at his sides are eight Bodhisattvas, the "Beings of Enlightenment", depicted in beauty and brilliantly garbed. Each, like the Buddha himself, has a nimbus. The Bodhisattvas are standing, in groups of four. Silk a deep dark brown, considerably worn and showing some cracks. Vestiges of seal marks at lower left, unreadable.

notes.label: Marks
notes.content: Vestiges of seal marks at lower left, unreadable. One seal, undecipherable.

notes.label: Label
notes.content: Amitabha, known in Korean as Amita-bul, the Buddha who promises salvation to all believers, is seated in the center of a goup of eight bodhisattvas (enlightened beings). The Buddha wears a red robe embelished with gold patterns, while all but one of the bodhisattvas wear jeweled crowns and fine, translucent garments. Only one, Kshitigarbha, who has the power to save even those who have been reborn in Hell, wears a simpler, hooded garment. Under court patronage Korean Buddhist art of the Koryo dynasty (918-1392) developed an extraordinarily refined style.
